name: prospective_students
title: Bellini prospective students: AI entry and transfer requirements

rules.title: First-year entry and preparation
rules.summary: Bellini first-year entry is in fall or spring. AI applicants need a strong record including four years of advanced mathematics and science including chemistry and physics; additional preparatory coursework may be necessary. University admission does not remove program-specific catalog conditions.

rules.title: Math placement and prior calculus credit
rules.summary: New first-year students must pass basic and college algebra placement; prior high-school precalculus/calculus adds the precalculus/trigonometry exam. Each passing score is 12 of 15. Passing all three supports starting Calculus I in fall; existing Calculus I credit is exempt. The page’s reference to students unable to complete “the course” does not identify a blanket placement-failure dismissal rule.

rules.title: Transfer admission level
rules.summary: Lower-level transfer means 12–29 prior postsecondary credit hours, mid-level 30–59, and upper-level at least 60. These are admission cohorts, not undergraduate course levels.

rules.title: AI lower-level transfer admission
rules.summary: Require (SAT mathematics at least 570 OR ACT mathematics at least 24) AND high-school GPA at least 4.00 as calculated by Admissions. This is the explicitly shared Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence entry rule.

rules.title: AI mid/upper-level programming admission prerequisite
rules.summary: Complete Programming Concepts via COP 1220, COP 2030, COP 2224, COP 2360, COP 2510 or COP 2800 with at least C within at most two attempts. Transfer alternatives are not asserted to be six current USF offerings or six degree requirements.

rules.title: AI mid/upper-level mathematics and physics entry prerequisites
rules.summary: Complete Calculus I (MAC x281 or MAC x311), Calculus II (MAC x282 or MAC x312), and calculus-based Physics I with lab (PHY x048/PHY x048L or PHY x045/PHY x045L), each with at least C within at most two attempts. Wildcard codes remain as printed. The following Computer Engineering chemistry requirement and Cybersecurity/IT database, statistics and discrete-mathematics requirements do not apply through this AI section.

rules.title: Accelerated credit documentation
rules.summary: AP, IB, AICE, CAPE and dual-enrollment credit require official documents submitted to Admissions. Consult advising before retaking previously credited coursework; acceptance does not by itself establish AI requirement allocation.

rules.title: Transfer acceptance versus degree allocation
rules.summary: Admissions assesses transfer acceptance and recalculates GPA using all submitted transcripts. A transfer-credit summary does not establish allocation to degree requirements and excludes coursework still in progress when the transcript arrived.

rules.title: College and department allocation of transferred work
rules.summary: Out-of-state/private-institution courses are not guaranteed to satisfy either general education or major requirements. Departments review them individually; colleges determine degree applicability. Retain official course descriptions and syllabi. Degree Works allocation remains provisional until reviewed by advising or college personnel. This is a conditional approval procedure, not evidence that every proposed substitution is permitted.

rules.title: Public advising and authenticated forms
rules.summary: The public page directs students to Archivum for appointments and Canvas for advising schedules, mentoring, coaching, forms and applications. It does not publish the AI major’s detailed grade/progression standards. No authenticated student portal was accessed.
